active_exploratory_memories.hypothesis: For bathroom-specific target objects like soap bottles, prioritizing inspection of closed storage receptacles (e.g., cabinets) before open horizontal surfaces (e.g., countertops) reduces total search actions compared to the general open-surface-first heuristic.

probe_summary.evidence_goal: Whether the target object is located inside the first inspected closed storage receptacle, yielding fewer total navigation and interaction actions than if an open horizontal surface had been checked first.
probe_summary.local_function: Search available receptacles to locate and acquire the target object (soapbottle).
probe_summary.realization_pattern: visit a closed storage receptacle first, opening it if needed; if empty, visit an open horizontal surface next
stop_conditions: target object successfully taken into inventory
closed storage receptacle inspected and found empty, followed by open horizontal surface inspected
all available closed storage receptacles exhausted without finding target
inventory check confirms target is held

active_exploratory_memories.scope: ALFWorld pick-and-place tasks in bathroom environments where the target is a hygiene or toiletry item not immediately visible, and the room contains both open horizontal surfaces and closed storage receptacles typical of bathrooms.
